summary.prose: This Story closes CliProvider.runReadOnlySession's full tool-restriction gap for codex and vibe (claude's existing --allowedTools mechanism already works correctly and is untouched). Vibe's three independently-hardcoded, wrong tool-name lists become one corrected constant, with a check that the two intended analyze tools are actually present. Codex gains a native enabled_tools allowlist for insrc plus dynamic disabling of every other globally-registered server, discovered via a budgeted, cancellable `codex -C cwd mcp list --json` call -- and, before any of that, the session refuses to start if any directory from cwd to the filesystem root (other than the one layer whose own .codex/config.toml is, by exact path, the real global config file) declares its own mcp_servers table, since such a server cannot be enumerated or excluded by this Story's discovery mechanism.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

api.name: walkProjectMcpConfigLayers (new module-level helper)

parameters.name: cwd
parameters.purpose: the session's target working directory, the deepest layer to check

returns.meaning: true if cwd OR any ancestor directory up to the filesystem root, EXCLUDING only the one layer whose own .codex/config.toml path exactly equals the resolved global config file's path, has its own .codex/config.toml whose TOML-parsed `mcp_servers` value is a non-empty object, in any valid TOML form; false if no such layer exists

errors.condition: an existing, non-excluded .codex/config.toml at any checked layer cannot be read (non-ENOENT) or fails to parse as valid TOML

preconditions: none -- a pure presence check per layer, parsed with a real TOML parser; does not evaluate codex's own trust_level or layer-merge/override precedence
postconditions: resolves globalConfigPath = join(process.env.CODEX_HOME || join(homedir(), '.codex'), 'config.toml') ONCE; walks cwd to the filesystem root, and at each directory `dir` builds candidatePath = join(dir, '.codex', 'config.toml'); if candidatePath === globalConfigPath, that one layer is treated as clear WITHOUT being read (it is already fully handled by discoverCodexMcpServers) and the walk continues; every other layer is checked normally. This exact-path comparison -- not a directory-containment boundary -- correctly skips only the one default-case coincidence (confirmed live: at this environment's home directory, dir/.codex/config.toml literally equals the resolved global config path) while never wrongly excluding a genuine project layer when CODEX_HOME is configured inside a project tree (the two paths then never coincide, so nothing above or beside CODEX_HOME is skipped); when CODEX_HOME lies outside cwd's own ancestor chain entirely, the comparison simply never matches and the walk behaves as if no global config existed on this path

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: the dirname(CODEX_HOME)-boundary design (the prior round's fix) excludes the entire directory containing the global config and everything above it from the ancestor walk. Traced against the review's cited layout (CODEX_HOME=/work/repo/codex-state, cwd=/work/repo/src), this wrongly excludes /work/repo itself, so a genuine, distinct project-local .codex/config.toml at /work/repo would never be checked or refused.
migration.stateAfter: walkProjectMcpConfigLayers resolves the global config's own full file path once and walks cwd to the filesystem root, skipping (without reading) ONLY the one layer whose own .codex/config.toml path exactly equals that resolved global path; every other layer, including a project root above a CODEX_HOME nested inside the project tree, is checked normally. This single exact-path comparison correctly handles the default case, the CODEX_HOME-inside-project layout, and the CODEX_HOME-outside-cwd's-ancestor-chain case with no special-casing.

migrationSteps.action: change walkProjectMcpConfigLayers' exclusion logic from a directory-containment boundary to a single exact-path comparison against the resolved global config file
add the regression test using the review's exact cited layout (CODEX_HOME nested inside a project tree, sentinel at the project root triggers refusal, no sentinel leaves global insrc allowed)

migration.backwardCompat: walkProjectMcpConfigLayers is private/module-internal, introduced earlier in this Story's own design and not yet shipped -- this is a correction to that not-yet-released helper's own exclusion logic, not a change to any existing public API.

alternativesConsidered.name: Skip only the exact resolved global config file path; walk every ancestor to the filesystem root otherwise
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Replace the dirname(CODEX_HOME)-boundary exclusion with a precise comparison: resolve the global config's own full file path once (join(CODEX_HOME || join(homedir(),'.codex'), 'config.toml')), and while walking cwd to the filesystem root, skip (treat as clear) ONLY the one layer whose own '.codex/config.toml' path exactly equals that resolved global path -- every other layer, including ones above or beside it, is checked normally.
alternativesConsidered.approach: walkProjectMcpConfigLayers computes globalConfigPath once, then walks cwd upward to the filesystem root; at each directory it builds candidatePath = join(dir, '.codex', 'config.toml') and, if candidatePath === globalConfigPath, treats that one layer as clear without reading it (it is already fully handled by discoverCodexMcpServers) and continues the walk; every other candidatePath is read/parsed/checked as before.
pros: Correctly handles the default case (home directory's own .codex/config.toml IS the global config -- skipped) AND the review's cited CODEX_HOME-inside-project layout (the project root's .codex/config.toml is a DIFFERENT file from the global config at CODEX_HOME/config.toml, so it is never skipped and is still checked)
No special-casing needed for 'CODEX_HOME outside cwd's ancestor chain' -- the path comparison simply never matches, and the walk behaves exactly as if no global config existed on this path at all
Single exact-path comparison, not a directory-containment rule that can over-exclude
cons: Walks all the way to the filesystem root again (like the originally-withdrawn unbounded design), so a deep directory tree costs more filesystem I/O than the (incorrect) directory-boundary shortcut did -- though each check is a cheap stat/read, and typical repos are not deep enough for this to matter in practice

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the dirname(CODEX_HOME)-boundary exclusion (the withdrawn design)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: No change from the version this round's review rejected -- exclude the directory containing the global config and everything above it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Unchanged from the prior round's walkProjectMcpConfigLayers.
cons: Confirmed by direct trace to wrongly exclude a genuine project-local .codex/config.toml whenever CODEX_HOME is configured inside the project tree -- directly reproduces this round's HIGH finding
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Confirmed by direct trace to wrongly exclude a genuine project layer whenever CODEX_HOME sits inside the project tree -- directly reproduces this round's HIGH finding.

alternativesConsidered.name: Determine applicable project layers independently of CODEX_HOME entirely (e.g. stop only at a detected VCS/workspace root)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Instead of comparing against the global config's own path at all, bound or identify project layers using some other signal (a .git directory, a package.json, etc.) that does not reference CODEX_HOME.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace the global-config-path comparison with a heuristic project-root detector (first ancestor containing .git, or similar), and check only directories between cwd and that detected root.
pros: Would not depend on correctly resolving CODEX_HOME at all
cons: Invents a NEW boundary concept (a VCS/workspace root) that codex's own documented project-config precedence does not define or require -- this Story would be guessing at a rule codex itself does not state, rather than checking the one condition (identity with the global config file) that is actually well-defined and verifiable

Narrower than intended: a project-local .codex/config.toml OUTSIDE a detected VCS root (unusual but not excluded by codex's own documentation) would be missed entirely, trading one false-negative class for a different one
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Would avoid the CODEX_HOME dependency but invents an undocumented boundary concept and introduces its own, different false-negative class.
